sourceType: Official Government of Punjab tourism website
note: Facts extracted below; prose summaries are written in our own words, not copied verbatim from the source.
about: Northernmost Punjab district in the Majha region, between the Ravi and Beas rivers, bordering Pakistan. Officially designated 'City of Braves'. Named after Guriya Ji, a Sanwal Brahmin who founded the city in the early 17th century.

places.name: Gurdwara Sri Kandh Sahib, Batala
places.location: Batala town, 34 km from Amritsar (ATQ) airport; Batala Junction (BAT) railway station
places.facts: Marks the site where Guru Nanak Dev Ji was married to Mata Sulkhani in 1487.

places.name: Achleshwar Dham, Batala
places.location: Batala town, opposite Gurdwara Sri Kandh Sahib
places.facts: Ancient Hindu shrine dedicated to Kartik Ji, associated with the Satyug period; large annual Shivratri fair.

places.name: Chhota Ghallughara Memorial, Kahnuwan
places.location: Kahnuwan area, ~40 km from Gurdaspur town
places.facts: Marks the site of the Chhota Ghallughara (Minor Holocaust) of May 1746, where ~7,000 Sikhs were killed and 3,000 captured by Mughal forces.

places.name: Takht-i-Akbari, Kalanaur
places.location: Kalanaur town, ~26 km from Gurdaspur city
places.facts: Masonry coronation platform where Akbar was crowned on 14 February 1556 by regent Bairam Khan; ASI-protected; one of the few identifiable Mughal-era coronation sites in India.

places.name: Gurdwara Dera Baba Nanak
places.location: Dera Baba Nanak town, ~45 km from Gurdaspur city, ~1km from the India-Pakistan border
places.facts: Guru Nanak Dev Ji visited in 1515. Two Gurdwaras: Sri Darbar Sahib (golden dome built by Maharaja Ranjit Singh) and Sri Chola Sahib (preserves Guru Nanak's holy robe brought from Baghdad).

places.name: Mahakaleshwar Temple, Kalanaur
places.location: Kalanaur town, ~26 km from Gurdaspur city
places.facts: Shiva temple with a horizontal Shivalinga, said to be the only such temple in India; large annual Shivratri fair.

places.name: Sri Kartarpur Sahib Corridor, Dera Baba Nanak
places.facts: Visa-free border corridor allowing Indian pilgrims to visit Gurdwara Darbar Sahib Kartarpur in Pakistan, where Guru Nanak Dev Ji spent his final years.

howToReach.air: Pathankot Airport (~43km) and Sri Guru Ram Dass Jee International Airport, Amritsar (~84km)
howToReach.road: PRTC/PUNBUS to Amritsar, Pathankot, Jalandhar, Chandigarh
